overview: The Medford City Council received updates from the MBTA on bus accessibility and from Eversource on utility paving, heard public testimony on union contract impasses and Winthrop Street parking, and passed six ordinances on third reading.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Winthrop Street residents expressed safety and parking concerns regarding proposed bike lanes, while Teamsters Local 25 reported contract negotiation impasses across eight city and school bargaining units.

items.title: 23-080 - Non-Union Personnel Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Received and placed on file a communication from the mayor requesting to amend the non-union personnel ordinance for the Human Resources Director position.

items.title: 23-081 - MBTA Bus Stop Accessibility and Elimination Presentation
items.summary: Tabled to April 25 a presentation on MBTA bus stop accessibility upgrades and stop eliminations while requesting rectangular rapid flashing beacons at several intersections.

items.title: 23-028 - Eversource Underground Cable and Paving Update
items.summary: Received an update from Eversource on completed cable pulling, sidewalk ramp construction, and nighttime milling and paving plans.

items.title: 23-076, 23-077, 23-078, 23-079 - Resolutions and Ceremonial Business
items.summary: Approved resolutions extending best wishes for Ramadan, expressing condolences for Marguerite Aguido, recognizing Walk, Bike, and Roll to School Day, and celebrating Women's History Month.

items.title: Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the records of March 21, 2023, along with committee reports on a budget process ordinance and a condominium conversion ordinance.

items.title: 23-082 - Ordinance Legal Review Status and City Solicitor Vacancy
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update on council ordinances lacking city solicitor review and requesting administration funding for a per-diem solicitor.

items.title: Third Reading of Pending Ordinances
items.summary: Passed on third reading six ordinances covering Community Preservation Act amendments, housing stability notifications, public surveillance oversight, a stormwater revolving fund, an affordable housing trust, and the Traffic and Transportation Director position.
